methodology_note: Study units derived from Toronto Notes SOURCE STRUCTURE (toc_inventory.json / derived/scope_packets/MG.json), cross-verified against the canonical raw-OCR corpus (derived/toronto-notes-2025/clean-ocr/, pdf pages 779-790) given this chapter's TOC-extraction pattern of garbled section titles and only two LOW-confidence, TOC_OCR_UNANCHORED T-children per section (a pattern already seen in chapters GY/H/ID). Findings: (1) MG.S01's printed title 'AcromymS' (OCR-garbled) is confirmed via merged_duplicate_headings to actually be 'Introduction to Genetics' (pdf 780-781/MG2-3: Common Terms - penetrance, expressivity, genetic/phenotypic heterogeneity, mosaicism; Triplet Repeat Expansions; Imprinting Disorders; Mitochondrial Disorders), with the genuine 'Pedigrees' T-child body-confirmed at pdf 781/MG3 (not MG2 as the node's own start_pdf_page would suggest) and 'Genetic Testing and Counselling' body-confirmed at pdf 782/MG4 (one page later than the parent node's recorded end_pdf_page of 781) - both T-children carry corrected EXACT_TOPIC page precision rather than the packet's implicit inheritance. (2) MG.S02.T01 'Congenital Anomalies' is body-confirmed at pdf 782/MG4, immediately after the 'Differences in Morphology' section heading; MG.S02.T02 'Approach to the Patient with Physical Differences' is body-confirmed at pdf 783/MG5. (3) The largest structural gap: MG.S03 ('GeneticConditions', pdf 784-788/MG6-10) contains four substantial, real subsections with NO corresponding toc_inventory.json T-child - Table 2 (Common Chromosomal Aneuploidy Syndromes: Trisomy 21/18/13), Table 3 (Sex Chromosome Disorders: Fragile X, Klinefelter, Turner), Table 4 (Other Genetic Syndromes: 22q11.2/DiGeorge, Prader-Willi, Angelman, Noonan, CHARGE), and Table 5 (Familial Cancer Syndromes) - all confirmed at pdf 784-785/MG6-7, preceding the genuine 'Other Single Gene Disorders' T-child heading (also body-confirmed, at pdf 785/MG7, not MG6). This is the same class of defect already documented in chapters GY, H, and ID (a real subheading merged into or dropped ahead of a recorded T-child), here affecting four distinct high-yield topic clusters rather than one. Each is represented as its own study unit citing the parent node MG.S03, per the GY-Fibroids/H-Sickle-Cell/ID-Endemic-Mycoses dual/multi-unit precedent, rather than being folded uncredited into 'Other Single Gene Disorders'. (4) Within the genuine 'Other Single Gene Disorders' T-child (pdf 785-787/MG7-9), Sickle Cell Disease and Cystic Fibrosis are themselves pure cross-reference entries ('see Hematology, H21'; 'More information found in other chapters'), while Wilson Disease, Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy, and Tay-Sachs Disease carry substantial independent narrative content - represented as four separate units (one REFERENCE_ONLY, three DIRECT) sharing the same source node, per the cross-reference-only-entry precedent already used in chapter ID (SU-ID-06/23/28). (5) MG.S03.T02 'Metabolic Diseases' is body-confirmed at pdf 787/MG9 (not pdf 784 as the parent node's start_pdf_page would suggest), continuing into Table 8 and the Initial Investigations content at pdf 788/MG10. All findings were resolved via the canonical clean-ocr corpus (derived/toronto-notes-2025/clean-ocr/, pdf pages 779-790), never via model memory. No heading was invented: every study unit below cites an actual toc_inventory.json node id; no UNCATALOGUED synthetic ids were required for this chapter.

organizational_header_nodes.MG: Chapter root container - represented by all study units below, per the C/ELOM/A/CP/D/E/FM/G/GS/GM/GY/H/ID convention.

study_units.title: Genetic Terminology (Penetrance, Expressivity, Heterogeneity, Mosaicism)
study_units.structural_rationale: MG.S01's printed title 'AcromymS' (OCR-garbled 'Acronyms') carries merged_duplicate_headings 'Introduction to Genetics'; body-confirmed at pdf 780/MG2 as a 'Common Terms' glossary (penetrance, expressivity, genetic/allelic/locus/phenotypic heterogeneity, mosaicism). Represented as a standalone vocabulary unit, separate from the non-Mendelian inheritance-pattern content on the following page (SU-MG-02), since these terms are foundational definitions rather than an independently testable competency.

study_units.title: Non-Mendelian Inheritance Patterns (Triplet Repeat Expansion/Anticipation, Imprinting/Uniparental Disomy, Mitochondrial Inheritance)
study_units.structural_rationale: Continuation of MG.S01's true 'Introduction to Genetics' content (see SU-MG-01); body-confirmed at pdf 781/MG3: Triplet Repeat Expansions (genetic anticipation; e.g. Fragile X, Huntington disease), Imprinting Disorders (parent-of-origin expression, uniparental disomy; e.g. Prader-Willi, Angelman, Beckwith-Wiedemann), and Mitochondrial Disorders. Split from SU-MG-01 because these are recognizable, independently testable inheritance-pattern concepts rather than pure vocabulary.

study_units.title: Pedigree Analysis
study_units.structural_rationale: Node MG.S01.T01 ('Pedigrees', LOW-confidence TOC_OCR_UNANCHORED) is body-confirmed as a genuine heading at pdf 781/MG3, not at the parent node's own start_pdf_page (780/MG2). Covers pedigree symbol conventions and the inclusion of sex-assigned-at-birth/gender-identity considerations when counselling gender-diverse patients and families.

study_units.title: Genetic Testing and Counselling
study_units.structural_rationale: Node MG.S01.T02 ('Genetic Testing and Counselling', LOW-confidence TOC_OCR_UNANCHORED) is body-confirmed as a genuine heading at pdf 782/MG4 - one page after the parent MG.S01 node's own recorded end_pdf_page (781) - covering presymptomatic testing, newborn screening, preconception counselling, preimplantation genetic diagnosis, and Table 1 (Common Genetic Tests: karyotype, FISH, microarray, Sanger, NGS, MLPA, PCR).

study_units.title: Congenital Anomalies: Classification and Mechanisms
study_units.structural_rationale: MG.S02 ('Differences inMorphology') and its T01 child 'Congenital Anomalies' are body-confirmed together at pdf 782/MG4: minor vs. major anomalies; mechanisms (malformation, disruption, deformation, dysplasia); and multiple-anomaly patterns (association, sequence, syndrome; e.g. VACTERL, Potter sequence, CHARGE).

study_units.title: Approach to the Patient with Physical Differences (Dysmorphology Assessment)
study_units.structural_rationale: Node MG.S02.T02 is body-confirmed at pdf 783/MG5: general approach (major/minor anomaly, mechanism, association/sequence/syndrome, familial recurrence), history (in-text cross-references to Obstetrics OB4 for teratogenic exposures and Pediatrics P26 for developmental history), and a systematic dysmorphology physical exam (facial gestalt, ears, eyes, philtrum, spine, hands).

study_units.title: Chromosomal Aneuploidy Syndromes (Trisomy 21, 18, 13)
study_units.structural_rationale: Table 2 (Common Chromosomal Aneuploidy Syndromes: Down syndrome/Trisomy 21, Edwards syndrome/Trisomy 18, Patau syndrome/Trisomy 13) is body-confirmed at pdf 784/MG6, directly under the MG.S03 'GeneticConditions' umbrella heading with no dedicated toc_inventory.json T-child of its own - it precedes the genuine 'Other Single Gene Disorders' T-child (body-confirmed one page later, at pdf 785/MG7). Represented as its own unit citing the parent node, per the GY-Fibroids/H-Sickle-Cell/ID-Endemic-Mycoses precedent for real content merged ahead of a recorded T-child.

study_units.title: Sex Chromosome Disorders and Fragile X Syndrome (Turner Syndrome, Klinefelter Syndrome, Fragile X Syndrome)
study_units.structural_rationale: Table 3 (Common Genetic Disorders Involving the Sex Chromosomes: Fragile X, Klinefelter, Turner syndromes) is body-confirmed at pdf 784/MG6, immediately following Table 2 (see SU-MG-07), under the same MG.S03 umbrella with no dedicated T-child. Represented as a separate unit given its distinct testable content (sex-chromosome aneuploidy and the FMR1 trinucleotide-repeat mechanism introduced in SU-MG-02).

study_units.title: Microdeletion and Other Recognizable Genetic Syndromes (22q11.2/DiGeorge Syndrome, Prader-Willi Syndrome, Angelman Syndrome, Noonan Syndrome, CHARGE Syndrome)
study_units.structural_rationale: Table 4 (Examples of Other Genetic Syndromes) is body-confirmed at pdf 784/MG6, immediately following Table 3 (see SU-MG-08), under the same MG.S03 umbrella with no dedicated T-child.

study_units.title: Familial Cancer Syndromes (Li-Fraumeni, Lynch, FAP, Hereditary Breast/Ovarian Cancer, Von Hippel-Lindau, Cowden, Neurofibromatosis)
study_units.structural_rationale: Table 5 (Examples of Familial Cancer Syndromes) is body-confirmed at pdf 785/MG7, under the same MG.S03 umbrella with no dedicated T-child, immediately preceding the genuine 'Other Single Gene Disorders' T-child heading on the same page (see SU-MG-11 through SU-MG-14).

study_units.title: Cross-Referenced Single-Gene Disorders (Sickle Cell Disease, Cystic Fibrosis)
study_units.structural_rationale: Within the genuine 'Other Single Gene Disorders' T-child (body-confirmed at pdf 785/MG7, one page after the parent node's own start_pdf_page of 784), Sickle Cell Disease is a single-line cross-reference ('see Hematology, H21') and Cystic Fibrosis is explicitly marked 'More information found in other chapters' - both carry zero independent MG-chapter content, per the same cross-reference-only-entry pattern used in chapter ID (SU-ID-06/23/28).

study_units.title: Wilson Disease
study_units.structural_rationale: Body-confirmed at pdf 785/MG7 within 'Other Single Gene Disorders': autosomal recessive ATP7B pathogenic variant, impaired cellular copper transport, liver disease, movement disorders, Kayser-Fleischer rings, chelation therapy.

study_units.title: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
study_units.structural_rationale: Body-confirmed at pdf 785-786/MG7-8 within 'Other Single Gene Disorders': X-linked dystrophin-gene disorder; incidence, clinical features (Gowers' sign, pseudohypertrophy), diagnosis (molecular genetic studies, creatine kinase), and supportive management.

study_units.title: Tay-Sachs Disease
study_units.structural_rationale: Body-confirmed at pdf 787/MG9 within 'Other Single Gene Disorders': autosomal recessive HEXA pathogenic variant, elevated carrier frequency in specific populations (Ashkenazi Jewish, French Canadian, Cajun, Pennsylvania Dutch), classic infantile presentation with cherry-red macular spot.

study_units.title: Metabolic Diseases (Inborn Errors of Metabolism: General Approach, Newborn Screening, Acute Presentation)
study_units.structural_rationale: Node MG.S03.T02 ('Metabolic Diseases', LOW-confidence TOC_OCR_UNANCHORED) is body-confirmed at pdf 787/MG9 - not at the parent MG.S03 node's own start_pdf_page (784) - continuing into Table 8 (Metabolic Disorders) and the Initial Investigations for a Child with an Inborn Error of Metabolism at pdf 788/MG10.

study_units.title: Landmark Medical Genetics Trials
study_units.structural_rationale: Body-confirmed at pdf 789/MG11: landmark-trial summary table (phenylketonuria dietary management, elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor in cystic fibrosis) - bibliographic/evidence-summary material, consistent with the 'Landmark ... Trials' treatment already established in chapters A, C, CP, D, E, FM, GM, G.

study_units.title: References
study_units.structural_rationale: Chapter bibliography, confirmed at pdf 790/MG12; MG.S05.T01's title ('MGI Medical Genetics Toronto Notes 2025') is the recurring page-footer citation string rather than a distinct topic, consistent with the References-node treatment in all prior completed chapters.
